Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

trouble noun

misfortune; being in trouble

also in trouble, be in trouble, get into trouble, what’s the trouble?, troubles, be in difficulties, I’m expecting some big trouble, make big trouble for someone, be in a pickle, in a pickle, in a tight spot, have one’s hands full, be hard pressed, be in a fix, in a fix, in a pinch

classical

Ter. Ph. 193: nescio quod magnum hoc nūntiō exspectō malum
Traupman 110, 398

malum, malī n.

noun, second declension · Declension on Wiktionary

trouble, misfortune; (in comedy) a beating

“What’s the trouble?”: Quid istuc malī est? (Ter. Ph. 184, Heaut. 82; Plaut. Merc. 165); Traupman (p. 110) also gives Quid est negōtī? (see problem). To make trouble for someone, that is, punish him: malum dare alicui (Traupman 110).

Other words

  • labōrō, labōrāre, labōrāvī, labōrātum — be in trouble, be in difficulties

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 4.1.3: in rē autem familiārī … valdē labōrāmus; Traupman 110, 398 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    With in and the ablative of the matter; also of being ill (see suffer, from an illness).

  • angustiae, angustiārum f. pl. — a tight spot, difficulties

    noun, first declension, plural · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 11.3.3: is quoque in angustiīs est quīcum sumus; Traupman 305: (difficulty) angustiae; Traupman 105: to be in a pickle, in angustiīs versor · Declension on Wiktionary

  • satis agere — have one’s hands full, be hard pressed

    also used · classical · Gell. 3.8.1: satisque agerent Rōmānī (Lewis & Short s.v. satis); Cic. Att. 4.15.9: pugnātur ācriter: agitur tamen satis (Lewis & Short)

    Lewis & Short: “to have enough to do, have one’s hands full; to be in trouble”. Impersonal, agitur satis, it is a hard struggle. Traupman 99 gives agitur satis for “things are going fairly well”, which it does not mean (see so-so).

Examples

  • Quid istuc malī est?

    What’s the trouble?Ter. Ph. 184

  • Nescio quod magnum hoc nūntiō exspectō malum.

    With this news I expect some big trouble.Ter. Ph. 193

  • in rē autem familiārī, quae quem ad modum frācta, dissipāta, dīrepta sit nōn ignōrās, valdē labōrāmus

    but with my money, which, as you know, has been broken up, scattered and plundered, I am in real troubleCic. Att. 4.1.3

  • Dare magnum malum alicui.

    To make big trouble for someone.Traupman 110

  • In angustiīs versor.

    I’m in a pickle.Traupman 105

  • in angustiīs versārī

    to be in a fixTraupman 316

  • in rē dubiā

    in a pinch (in a doubtful situation)Traupman 360

  • aliquem in aerumnam obserere

    to get someone into troubleTraupman 398

  • Quid illuc malī est?

    What’s the trouble?Traupman 398

See also problem, trouble, what’s the matter?, so-so.
